title: Strategic Insights from HSBC’s CIO for Southeast Asia and India, Global Private Banking and Wealth: James Cheo on Navigating Global Investment Markets - Hubbis
text:
Exit Full Page Articles Investments Strategic Insights from HSBC’s CIO for Southeast Asia and India, Global Private Banking and Wealth: James Cheo on Navigating Global Investment Markets Investments Strategic Insights from HSBC’s CIO for Southeast Asia and India, Global Private Banking and Wealth: James Cheo on Navigating Global Investment Markets James Cheo of HSBC Bank Jun 3, 2024 Download PDF View Event Hubbis recently enjoyed an insightful and informative discussion with James Cheo, the Singapore-based Chief Investment Officer, SE Asia and India, for HSBC Global Private Banking & Wealth. James shed light on the nuances of investor psychology amidst fluctuating interest rates in the US and Europe, provided strategic insights into current investment opportunities in bond and equity markets, and evaluated the long-term implications of technological advances such as artificial intelligence on global economies and markets. He advocated that investors take a longer-term portfolio formation view and shift from cash to investments, promoting the 50/50 or 60/40 portfolio, with fixed income compelling in light of rates that should gradually fall (albeit perhaps not imminently), and with equities high in the US but still present opportunities, especially related to AI, and with buying opportunities emerging at times of weakness amidst ongoing volatility. He also pointed to the merits of alternative and private assets as valuable mid to long-term diversification opportunities. His overall advice was that investors should pursue smart, balanced strategies amid the complex global financial landscape, crafting portfolios that are resilient and responsive to both current trends and potential future shifts. James opens the discussion by highlighting the current investor psychology, noting that clients' primary concerns revolve around interest rate predictions—specifically, the timing and magnitude of potential rate cuts in the US and also Europe. He notes that while there is a prevailing belief that rate cuts are imminent, the actual number of cuts, whether two or three in 2024, will largely depend on the actual inflation data. However, he remains optimistic, suggesting that, regardless of the specifics, a series of rate reductions are expected within the next one to two years. Cash is no longer king Regarding current investment strategies, James explains that this rate scenario means that clients are actively looking to put their cash to work, particularly by investing initially in bond markets. Some are considering extending the duration of their bonds as a strategic move in anticipation of these rate cuts. This strategy aims to capitalise on the current higher yields before they potentially decrease following the rate cuts, as well as position portfolios for fixed-income capital appreciation as rates fall. James advises against being overly cautious or reactive to sensational headlines. Instead, he suggests that this period should be viewed as an opportunity to deploy cash into investments, particularly given the compelling bond yields currently available. Volatility can offer opportunities He adds that the current volatility in major financial markets should be seen as an opportunity to build a more diversified investment portfolio that includes rising exposures to equities. He points to the continuing strong interest in the US equity market, which continues to attract attention from investors looking to balance their portfolios with additional equity allocations. On this point, James addresses concerns about the high valuation of US equities, particularly within the technology sector, which seems concentrated around a few mega stocks. He does not see this as an overt negative, noting the importance of focusing on the tech sector, especially given the impact of artificial intelligence (AI), which he views as a continuing multi-year trend. Specifically, he highlights the success of chip makers and cloud providers who enable AI technology, stating that these sectors have performed well and are likely to continue thriving due to the ongoing demand for AI computing capabilities. AI as a key catalyst Looking forward, James believes the next phase of growth in the equity market will involve AI adopters—companies that integrate AI models into their end-to-end processes to gain a competitive edge. He predicts that the benefits of AI will extend beyond the tech sector into non-tech sectors, making it a key area for potential investment opportunities. This transition, however, might be challenging to pinpoint and is expected to unfold over several years. In addition, he suggests that the broader economic data supports a strong case for continued investment in equities, particularly if a soft-landing scenario plays out, as many anticipate. He predicts this could lead to a broadening of the equity market rally, extending gains beyond the currently dominant sectors. China – fiscal and monetary policies key to recovery James discusses the current status of and outlook for Chinese equities, noting that his stance is neutral currently. He acknowledges the complexity of China's economic situation, highlighting the recent Q1 GDP growth of 5.3%, which surpassed expectations. Despite this positive indicator, James points out that the Chinese economy is not performing optimally across all sectors. The property market, in particular, remains weak and continues to be a significant drag on the economy and the financial markets, although the situation has improved slightly compared to the past couple of years. Additionally, James remarks on the mixed signals from other Chinese economic indicators. Retail sales are showing signs of improvement but are not as robust as anticipated. Similarly, industrial production is rising but has not experienced the sharp V-shaped recovery many hoped for. Given these factors, James suggests that while China will likely meet its growth targets, achieving and maintaining this growth will require increased governmental support through fiscal and monetary policies to sustain the momentum. Long-term, global and diversified On the topic of geopolitics and its impact on investment advice and client actions, James admits that there is no simple solution to hedge a portfolio completely against geopolitical risks. Addressing the common behaviour of Asian private clients, who often actively manage their investments DIY and are often active traders, James advises adopting a long-term investment strategy, advocating a globally diversified portfolio. He typically supports the traditional balanced approach of a 50-50 or 60-40 equity-bond portfolio. However, he suggests enhancing this strategy by incorporating alternatives to increase portfolio resilience. Alternatives beckon He explains that due to the high volatility in equity markets and the increasing correlation between equities and bonds, it is prudent to integrate uncorrelated assets such as private equity and private credit. These alternatives can complement traditional public equities and bonds, offering more stable and diversified returns. This approach, he believes, will help investors construct more resilient portfolios for the long term. He expands on the importance of alternative investments like hedge funds, venture capital, private equity, private credit, infrastructure, and commodities in modern investment strategies. He advises investors to consider this entire spectrum of alternatives to achieve diversification benefits that enhance portfolio resilience. Specifically, he notes that hedge funds, despite varying performance records, remain relevant due to their diverse strategies and says commodities should not be overlooked. However, he advocates maintaining a globally diversified portfolio as the most effective strategy to navigate such uncertainties. He highlights that including alternatives in a portfolio can provide additional protection against geopolitical fluctuations. For example, investing with hedge fund managers who can capitalise on market dislocations or in commodities that might benefit from geopolitical tensions can be advantageous. James underscores the importance of building a resilient portfolio to withstand market volatility and geopolitical risks, encouraging continued investment rather than retreating to cash. Measures of success… James discusses how he assesses his team’s performance, likening his role to "climbing up the mast of a ship trying to look out for opportunities while at the same time with a keen eye to avoid dangers.” He says he evaluates their success based on their collective ability to educate and lead clients towards creating healthier, more resilient, and more diversified portfolios. He adds that many Asian-based clients have a strong home or local bias in their investments and that he strives to counterbalance this inclination by identifying global investment opportunities and encouraging a shift in both action and mindset among his clientele. Asia’s demographics Addressing some specific trends among the massing ranks of younger clients in Asia, James observes that they are increasingly savvy and seek holistic wealth management. “The second, third and even further generation investors demand credible data for better analysis and are particularly focused on sustainability,” he reports. “They are increasingly interested in understanding the carbon intensity of their portfolios and aligning their investments with global standards like the Paris Agreement, reflecting a gradual but noticeable shift in their investment approach.” Keeping it simple Expanding on this and shifting to client engagement, he points to the challenge of information overload and the importance of delivering concise, insightful content that cuts through the noise. He emphasises the necessity of providing well-researched, easily digestible information that offers clear action points, and moving away from lengthy reports to more focused communications that cater to the typical clients' evolving preferences. In a highly competitive market where investment products are largely similar across the private banks, James identifies the "house view" as a key differentiator that helps establish the credibility of the entire investment process and proposition. He stresses the importance of accuracy in research, noting that consistent errors can erode client and relationship manager (RM) confidence. "Accuracy, integrity and quality are vital for confidence, not only amongst clients but amongst sales teams, RMs, advisors and the entire team,” he states. “We are pleased to share that our Singapore-based research team has been awarded with Singapore’s Best for Investment Research by Euromoney Global Private Banking Awards 2024.” At your service James expands the conversation to their discretionary portfolio management (DPM) offering for Global Private Banking clients, noting that these portfolios reflect the house view but are tailored to individual client needs through different models. He explains that HSBC Discretionary Portfolio Management is tailored for investors who need to prioritise their time yet want to ensure their investments are actively managed. “By entrusting HSBC with day-to-day investment responsibilities, clients retain control over the mandate's parameters while gaining the peace of mind to focus on other life priorities,” James elucidates. “Leveraging a global network of over 500 investment professionals across 30 countries, we can help clients expertly navigate the complex investment universe of equities, fixed income, funds, and alternative investments to meet client objectives.” DPM’s virtues He adds that the foundation of HSBC's DPM offering for Global Private Banking clients is built on four key principles: dynamic asset allocation to drive performance, rigorous rebalancing to optimise risk and returns, stringent risk management to align with your tolerance levels, and a commitment to cost efficiency by securing competitive fees. This comprehensive approach ensures that client investments are not only well-managed but also aligned with your financial goals and risk preferences,” James says. He contrasts this DPM approach with pure advisory services, where clients may choose to make their own trading decisions based on HSBC’s advice provided. But James says he believes the optimal solution for clients in Asia often lies between these two approaches, highlighting their solution in the form of HSBC’s hybrid model called "Prism," which combines portfolio advisory with powerful risk engine analytics from BlackRock’s Aladdin. Eyes on the Prism Offering more detail, he adds that HSBC Prism Advisory is a holistic portfolio-based advisory and investment service for Global Private Banking clients that combines expert guidance and data-driven insights. HSBC uses institutional-quality portfolio and risk analytics provided by Aladdin Wealth technology from BlackRock. “We link our strategic and tactical views to our global investment capabilities and opportunities,” he explains, “so clients can manage investments with high-quality, timely, and personalised advice. With 3,000+ risk factors monitored daily, Aladdin Wealth technology drives portfolio transparency for advisors to deliver a more disciplined investment approach to clients.” “Prism is a great example of how we are combining technology with the expertise of our people to deliver our investment content and portfolio advice – and ultimately helping clients make more informed decisions according to their objectives,” he reports. Key Priorities James expresses a key goal of continuing to lead investment research and aspires to be recognised again as the best research house in Singapore. This ambition underpins his broader objective to maintain credibility and accuracy in communicating the firm's house view. Furthermore, he reiterates their strategic focus on deploying client cash effectively, particularly in light of anticipated interest rate cuts. He envisions this year as a pivotal moment for investment opportunities, advocating using discretionary portfolios, perhaps the hybrid ‘Prism’ platform, or even client-directed investments as long as the end result is truly robust and diversified portfolios. “The ultimate aim is to assist clients in more effectively navigating the market dynamics, leveraging disciplined and sharp research, AI, and other advances to enhance our judgement and advice while boosting operational efficiency and elevating decision-making in our investment management and advisory services,” says James. Seeing the big picture James’ extensive overview reflects a comprehensive approach to investment that blends rigorous analysis with strategic foresight to create a big-picture view of the challenges and objectives ahead. “Ultimately, our mission is to deliver informed analysis and advice that clients can understand easily and act upon with real confidence,” he states. “No investment advice is perfect, as this is an imperfect world, and markets are so often unpredictable, and there are unforeseen surprises. But we hope and believe that our rigorous, longer-term yet agile approach sets us and our clients on the right path.” Getting Personal with James Cheo James, born and raised in Singapore, studied Business and Finance at Nanyang Technological University, and graduated with a first-class honours degree. He started his career at Singapore's central bank, where he carved out a niche for himself specialising in data analysis, focusing on network models and stress tests. This work became especially critical during the global financial crisis, helping him transition from a data analyst in the background to a more visible and strategic role. After five years with the Monetary Authority of Singapore, James briefly joined a family office. Soon thereafter, he joined HSBC in 2010 as an investment strategist. His career included periods at Barclays and the Bank of Singapore, where he gained more experience and responsibility. Outside of his professional life, James is deeply committed to his family. Married with three children, he enjoys being actively involved in their lives, often jokingly referring to himself as a weekend 'cab driver' for them. His personal interests include a passion for reading, particularly in financial history, which was highlighted by a recent meeting with the historian Niall Ferguson, an author he greatly admires. Travel is another important aspect of his life. A recent family trip to Korea was not only a welcome break from his routine but also an opportunity for cultural exploration and enjoying local cuisine, which James and his small tribe found delightful. By balancing his professional development with personal and family fulfilment, James's story is a testament to the equilibrium he strives to achieve between his career and life at home. His journey illustrates a commitment to professional excellence and personal growth, adventure, cohesion, and responsibility.
